name: Saint Martin of Tours
history: A Roman soldier who, at the gates of Amiens, cut his cloak in half for a freezing beggar and that night saw Christ wearing it. He became a monk and bishop of Tours, one of the first saints venerated who was not a martyr. His feast fell on the day the 1918 Armistice was signed.
fast: Martinmas once began 'Saint Martin's Lent', a forty-day fast before Christmas. Consider an Advent discipline beginning today.
meditation: Whom will you give half your cloak to this week?
life: Martin was born around 316 at Sabaria in Pannonia, in present-day Hungary, the son of an army officer, and grew up at Pavia. Drawn to Christ as a boy, he was enrolled in the cavalry at fifteen. After he shared his cloak with the beggar at Amiens he was baptised, and some time later he left the army, telling the emperor that he was now a soldier of Christ. He became a disciple of Saint Hilary of Poitiers and founded at Ligugé the first monastery known in Gaul. In 371 the people of Tours chose him as their bishop against his will. He lived as a monk at Marmoutier outside the city, travelled the countryside preaching, and was known for his care of prisoners and the poor. He died at Candes in 397. His life was written by his friend Sulpicius Severus.
prayerTo: Saint Martin, soldier of Christ, you saw the Lord in a freezing beggar and gave him half of what you had. Pray for soldiers and for all who suffer the cost of war, and for me, that I may not pass by the poor but share with them freely, as Christ has shared Himself with me. Amen.
penance: Give a warm coat or blanket to a shelter or clothing bank today, and pray for those who have died in war.
prayer: O God, Who see that we cannot survive by any power of our own, mercifully grant that, by the intercession of blessed Martin, Your Confessor and Bishop, we may be made safe from all harm. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
